hypotheses.name: OS descheduling
hypotheses.signature: Analyze continuous wall/threadCPU paired differences and distribution shifts. Moderate/severe flags follow statistics.H1_event_rules; runnable offCPU trace required for descheduling, never wall-minusCPU alone.
hypotheses.control: D system_trace_background: fixed one busy helper on/off; B no induced load
hypotheses.weakens: CPU rises proportionally; no traced runnable wait
hypotheses.sufficient: >=3 query-linked events in >=2sessions, uncertainty-valid runnable offCPU trace explaining dominant excess, blocked waits separated; 80% accounting and50% controlled intervention are engineering heuristics defined in H1_event_rules, not confidence guarantees. Missing direct support =>UNRESOLVED.
hypotheses.limit: without scheduler trace only off-CPU component, cause unresolved

hypotheses.name: CPU execution-time regression
hypotheses.signature: matched work and higher threadCPU duration, not just wall
hypotheses.control: randomized frozen binaries P1/P2 and B mirrored diagnostics; D trace-off control
hypotheses.alternative: core/frequency or memory stalls rather than more instructions
hypotheses.weakens: CPU stable while elapsed spikes; diagnostic asymmetry
hypotheses.sufficient: valid B native-threadCPU NRp99 ratio lower secondary-family Bonferroni bound >1 for affected region/protocol, direction in >=6/8 sessions and corroborated uninstrumented A elapsed regression; causal software attribution additionally needs mechanism/control in D
hypotheses.limit: on-CPU time includes stalled cycles and does not prove algorithm-work change

hypotheses.name: Frequency/core placement
hypotheses.signature: query-thread trace shows P/E migration or execution placement and calibrated temporally relevant performance-state evidence
hypotheses.control: repeated matched work/order across sessions; trace-on/off; no claimed hard pinning
hypotheses.alternative: background contention, cache effects, changing QoS
hypotheses.weakens: same validated core/state with persistent CPU excess
hypotheses.sufficient: direct query-synchronized placement/state plus replicated controlled isolation of alternatives; cluster frequency alone insufficient
hypotheses.limit: no safe public per-query frequency control established; likely unresolved if available telemetry is aggregate

hypotheses.name: Background workload
hypotheses.signature: temporal runnable delays or memory contention associated with known helper/background activity
hypotheses.control: D scheduler mode one fixed busy helper versus none, randomized balanced fresh subprocesses
hypotheses.alternative: helper also changes power/cache state; ordinary background different
hypotheses.weakens: no repeatable helper effect or no temporal overlap
hypotheses.sufficient: matched intervention effect interval excludes zero, repeats >=2 sessions with same signature as ordinary events; cannot retroactively identify historical background process
hypotheses.limit: only causal for specified helper intervention; natural-process correlations alone weak

hypotheses.name: Allocator latency
hypotheses.signature: query-tagged slow request/free interval accounts for excess, with wall/CPU and non-nested inclusive accounting
hypotheses.control: C count-only versus timed requests; same source/permutation/variant; D allocation stacks as fixed companion trace on C sessions0/2
hypotheses.alternative: descheduling inside allocator call, recursive logging, wrapper perturbation
hypotheses.weakens: request duration negligible; events disappear only when hook active; counts differ
hypotheses.sufficient: same-source per-event durations/stacks, >=80% excess accounting without double counting, >=3 events in >=2 sessions; temporally matching wait/CPU evidence and corroboration without wrapper; otherwise allocator-associated only
hypotheses.limit: no allocator replacement/optimization or causal claim from aggregate byte totals

hypotheses.name: Cache/TLB/memory access
hypotheses.signature: validated query-attributed exported memory bottleneck metrics shift with CPU excess
hypotheses.control: D cpu_counters_cache: 64MiB fixed 64-byte-stride buffer touch before query versus retained-hot run; same untimed preparation for both variants
hypotheses.alternative: preconditioning changes power and allocator/page state; interference
hypotheses.weakens: no supported metric shift or stable CPU cost under conditioning
hypotheses.sufficient: supported metrics, preserved units/core mapping, repeated controlled effect plus alternatives addressed; TLB-specific attribution requires actual validated TLB event

H1_event_rules.labels: abs(deltaW)>=severe =>severe; moderate<=abs(deltaW)<severe =>moderate; remainder retained as continuous observations. sign records slower variant. Exactly at threshold is included.
H1_event_rules.historical_extreme_flag: W_variant>max(1.5*H,H+0.010), parent flag retained separately, not an H1 entry requirement
H1_event_rules.continuous_analysis: all observations, signed paired wall/CPU/nonCPU deltas; separate full p50/p95/p99 ratios/differences, session summaries, source spreads and exceedance rates. Never threshold-filter distribution estimands.
H1_event_rules.offCPU_accounting: orient slow minus fast by sign(deltaW); E=abs(deltaW), Dcpu=CPUslow-CPUfast, Dgap=(Wslow-CPUslow)-(Wfast-CPUfast). Retain negative/components>100%; require E>epsilon. Use [Dgap-epsilon,Dgap+epsilon]/[E-epsilon,E+epsilon] conservatively, positive denominator. Dominance heuristic lower accounted fraction>=0.8 plus directly linked RUNNABLE offCPU intervals; blocked waits separately attributed.
H1_event_rules.heuristic_interpretation: 80% means predominantly accounted elapsed excess,50% means large reversible response to predeclared intervention; neither is statistical coverage, universal causal proof or automatic PASS. Require>=3events/>=2sessions, valid same-query trace/clock alignment and alternatives addressed.
H1_event_rules.uncertainty: clock/aperture bounds plus original cluster95% descriptive diagnostic intervals for controls; if interval/sign ambiguous, UNRESOLVED; thresholds alone never establish cause or resolve Task14F2
